title: Turn the lights back on promptly
text: Rolling outages are a last resort. When spare power climbs back above a safe cushion and supply is not falling, bring homes back gradually instead of keeping them dark just in case.

title: Never cut power to the gas supply
text: Most power plants burn gas. If outages switch off gas pumps and wells, plants lose fuel and outages grow. Protect gas facilities when cutting power, and winterize wells beforehand.

title: Weatherproof the power plants themselves
text: Protecting gas wells is not enough. If the plants freeze, the fuel has nowhere to go. Insulate and heat-trace power plants before winter so they keep running in deep cold.

title: Prepare early, shed ahead, restore promptly
text: When deep cold is forecast, line up extra plants, imports and conservation early. If supply is falling, shed a little ahead while keeping gas sites powered. Bring homes back as soon as reserves recover.

title: Prepare early, shed smart, restore promptly
text: Winterize before winter. When deep cold is forecast, commit units, import, and ask for conservation early. If supply is falling, shed ahead but protect gas facilities. Restore homes once reserves recover.

title: Prepare early, shed smart, restore promptly
text: Winterize before winter. When deep cold is forecast, commit units, import, and ask for conservation early. If supply is falling, shed ahead but protect gas facilities. Restore homes once reserves recover.

title: Bring homes back in bigger steps
text: Once reserves are comfortably above need, return homes in large steps. Do not wait for supply to stop wiggling. The bigger the spare power, the more homes come back each hour.

title: Spend winter money where freezing hurts
text: Most lost power came from frozen gas plants and wells. Put the winter budget there first instead of spreading it thinly over wind, coal and batteries.

title: Never hold homes dark with spare power
text: If reserves are comfortably above 15% and supply is not collapsing, keeping homes dark is needless. Bring a large block back right away.

title: Big outages with big reserves unwind
text: If many homes are dark while spare power is plentiful, bring them back steadily each hour. Darkness without a power shortage is a failure, not safety.

title: Restore whenever the cushion holds
text: Bring homes back in steady steps once reserves stay above a modest cushion and supply is not falling fast. Only cut ahead when reserves are truly thin.

title: Ask for more saving during outages
text: While some homes are dark, ask everyone else to save a bit more power. Every megawatt saved is a home that can be switched back on sooner.

title: Freeze-proof the plants that froze
text: Gas and coal plants froze and dragged supply down for days. Spend the winter budget finishing their weatherproofing rather than on backup fuel few plants used.

title: Fund freeze-proofing before backup fuel
text: Frozen wells and coal plants caused the shortfall, while backup fuel was rarely used. Move that money into weatherproofing wells and coal plants so less supply freezes when the cold peaks.

title: Protect wind turbines from icing
text: In deep cold most wind turbines iced up and stopped, the only fleet left unprotected. Weatherproofing part of it keeps more power flowing when demand peaks.
